goal: Verify that registration, login and JWT validation work correctly. The gateway protects endpoints and correctly proxies requests.
preconditions_global: Entire Docker stack is running (scenarios 0.1-0.2 passed)

variables_legend.$TOKEN: JWT token — copy from the access_token field after login
variables_legend.$ADMIN_TOKEN: Admin JWT token — copy after logging in as admin

scenarios.title: Register new user — happy path
scenarios.description: Creates a new account. Verify the response contains id and email, and that the password is not returned in plaintext.

steps.action: Send registration request with a valid email and password
steps.command: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/auth/register -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d $'{"email": "test@mail.com", "password": "test123"}' | python3 -m json.tool
steps.notes: Response MUST NOT contain a 'password' or 'hashed_password' field

scenarios.expected_outcome: HTTP 201, JSON with id/email/role, no password in response

scenarios.title: Registration — duplicate email (409)
scenarios.description: The system must not allow two accounts with the same email. Registering with the same email a second time should return an error.

steps.action: Try to register again with the same email
steps.command: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/auth/register -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d $'{"email": "test@mail.com", "password": "test456"}' | python3 -m json.tool
steps.notes: Code 409 Conflict. If you get 201 — deduplication is broken!

scenarios.expected_outcome: HTTP 409 with a duplicate error message

scenarios.title: Registration — invalid email (422)
scenarios.description: Pydantic validation should reject a string that is not a valid email.

steps.action: Send registration with an invalid email
steps.command: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/auth/register -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d $'{"email": "not-an-email", "password": "test123"}' | python3 -m json.tool

expected_response.detail: (list of Pydantic validation errors, 'email' field with message)

steps.notes: FastAPI automatically validates EmailStr — 422 Unprocessable Entity

scenarios.expected_outcome: HTTP 422 with email validation error details

scenarios.title: Registration — empty body (422)
scenarios.description: Verifies that missing required fields are validated.

steps.command: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/auth/register -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' | python3 -m json.tool

expected_response.detail: (validation errors for email and password fields)

scenarios.expected_outcome: HTTP 422 with list of missing fields

scenarios.title: Login — happy path + obtain JWT token
scenarios.description: Login returns a JWT token. The token is required for ALL subsequent tests — save it.

steps.command: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d $'{"email": "test@mail.com", "password": "test123"}' | python3 -m json.tool
steps.notes: Copy the access_token value — use it as $TOKEN in subsequent tests

steps.action: Save token in environment variable (optional — simplifies next commands)
steps.command: TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d $'{"email": "test@mail.com", "password": "test123"}' | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['access_token'])")
steps.expected_output: No output — token saved in $TOKEN variable
steps.notes: You can now use $TOKEN in the next curl commands in the same terminal session

scenarios.title: Login — wrong password (401)
scenarios.description: The system must not log in a user with a wrong password.

steps.action: Send login with an incorrect password
steps.command: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d $'{"email": "test@mail.com", "password": "wrongpassword"}' | python3 -m json.tool
steps.notes: The response SHOULD NOT reveal whether the email exists (timing attack). Ideally: same message as for a non-existent email.

scenarios.title: Login — non-existent user (401)
scenarios.description: Login with an email that does not exist in the database should also return 401 — the same message as for a wrong password.

steps.action: Send login with a non-existent email
steps.command: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d $'{"email": "ghost@mail.com", "password": "whatever"}' | python3 -m json.tool
steps.notes: Compare the message with test 1.6 — they should be identical so as not to reveal whether the email exists

scenarios.title: GET /auth/me — fetch logged-in user profile
scenarios.description: Protected endpoint that returns the currently logged-in user's data based on the JWT token.

steps.action: Fetch profile with JWT token in Authorization header
steps.notes: Replace $TOKEN with your token. Or use the variable if set in 1.5.

scenarios.title: GET /auth/me — without token (401)
scenarios.description: The /me endpoint is protected. Calling it without an Authorization header must return 401.

steps.notes: If you get 200 — the endpoint is not protected! This is a security bug.

scenarios.title: GET /auth/me — invalid token (401)
scenarios.description: A random string in the Authorization header must not be accepted as a token.

steps.action: Send request with a garbage token
steps.command: curl -s http://localhost:8000/auth/me -H 'Authorization: Bearer this.is.not.a.token' | python3 -m json.tool

scenarios.title: Admin seed — login with admin account
scenarios.description: On startup, the auth service automatically creates an admin account from .env values (ADMIN_EMAIL, ADMIN_PASSWORD). Verify it works and that the admin has role='admin'.
preconditions: Auth service is running (admin account seeded on startup)

steps.command: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d $'{"email": "admin@mail.com", "password": "admin"}' | python3 -m json.tool
steps.notes: Use ADMIN_EMAIL and ADMIN_PASSWORD values from your .env. Defaults: admin@mail.com / admin

steps.action: Save admin token and check the role
steps.command: ADMIN_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d $'{"email": "admin@mail.com", "password": "admin"}' | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['access_token'])") && curl -s http://localhost:8000/auth/me -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" | python3 -m json.tool

scenarios.title: Gateway — protect /admin/* endpoints without token (401)
scenarios.description: The gateway must block access to /admin/* endpoints without a JWT token.

steps.action: Try to access project list without a token
steps.notes: The gateway should reject the request before it reaches the admin service

scenarios.title: Gateway — access /admin/* with admin token (200)
scenarios.description: An admin with a valid token should have access to /admin/* endpoints.

steps.action: Fetch project list with admin token
steps.expected_response: (list of projects — may be empty [] on a clean database)
steps.notes: On a clean database returns an empty list. What matters is the status is 200, not 401/403.

scenarios.title: Gateway — unknown path (404)
scenarios.description: The gateway should return 404 for unknown paths instead of forwarding the request indefinitely.

scenarios.title: Gateway — routing /auth/* to auth service (proxy verification)
scenarios.description: Calls through the gateway on /auth/* reach the auth service. This verifies that the proxy works correctly.

steps.action: Login through gateway (port 8000) and directly through auth service (port 8001) — response should be identical
steps.command: echo '=== Via gateway (8000) ===' && curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d $'{"email": "test@mail.com", "password": "test123"}' | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print('token_type:', d.get('token_type'), '| has_token:', bool(d.get('access_token')))"
steps.notes: If you get a different result through the gateway than directly from auth — there is a proxy issue

scenarios.expected_outcome: Gateway and auth service directly return the same response format
